title: California
description: In California, there are no true education freedom options in which tax dollars follow the student. The only option is publicly controlled charter schools.
body:
# CURRENT GRADE: F

**There are no true education freedom options in which tax dollars follow the student. The only option is publicly controlled charter schools.**

**Homeschooling is not authorized under state statute. Families who want to homeschool must establish it as a private school with government oversight. There is also a vaccine mandate.**

**Compulsory education is for ages 6-18.**

# Education Options

[District of Choice](https://www.cde.ca.gov/sp/eo/dc/)

- This program permits students to attend public schools out of their district if the district school participates in the program.
- Districts are not required to participate.

[Charter Schools](https://www.cde.ca.gov/sp/ch/cefcharterschools.asp)

- These schools are still overseen by local school boards.
- May not be subject to all the same state laws and regulations as other public schools
- If applications exceed number of seats, students are chosen via lottery.
- Online charter schools are also an option but still provided by the government.

[Vaccine Mandate](https://choc.org/articles/immunization-guide/)

- California requires every child to be vaccinated for 10 diseases.
- There is no exemption for personal or religious belief.
- A medical exemption is permitted if authorized by a physician.
- This mandate is also for private school.

# Homeschooling Laws

### **Here are state laws on the topic of homeschooling:**

****

Here are [state requirements](https://www.cde.ca.gov/sp/ps/homeschool.asp) on the topic of homeschooling:

- California does not have a statute that authorizes home schooling.
- Some public schools offer independent study or home-based study as an option.
- In order to be exempt from public school attendance, parents must open their own private home-based program and meet [certain requirements](https://www.cde.ca.gov/sp/ps/psaffedcode.asp) such as record keeping (including vaccine requirements).
- Local district authority is over this exemption.
- Must instruct in the same subjects as public school.
- Attendance must be kept in a register (and shown to local attendance authorities).
- Must maintain a list of instructors.

**Religious Exemptions:**

The state has no formal laws related to religious exemptions.

The First Amendment states “Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, *or prohibiting the free exercise thereof*.” Many argue that a religious conviction to provide a home-based education is constitutionally protected and a state religious exemption law is not a requirement to be able to homeschool on religious grounds.

It should be noted that the U.S. Supreme Court in [*Wisconsin v. Yoder (1972)*](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/406/205/#tab-opinion-1949691) established that “Under the Free Exercise Clause of the First Amendment, a state law requiring that children attend school past eighth grade violates the parents’ constitutional right to direct the religious upbringing of their children.” (The case involved a challenge of a 16-year-old student to be exempt, so the scope was limited)
